quote: There is no cure for birth and death save to enjoy the interval.
source: George Santayana, Soliloquies in England and Later Soliloquies, 24, War Shrines (Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1922)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg ebook 48429, a transcription of the Scribner first American edition of 1922, read in full text; the Santayana Edition at IU Indianapolis gives p. 97 for the passage
evidence.edition: Soliloquies in England and Later Soliloquies, Charles Scribner’s Sons, New York, 1922
evidence.locator: soliloquy 24, War Shrines, following Wealth is dismal and poverty cruel unless both are festive

reason: The sentence stands whole and exact in War Shrines, numbered 24 in the table of contents of the 1922 Scribner edition. A complete sentence, not a cut, and Santayana has no line yet this year.
